title: Relationship and Depression Dynamics in Treatment: A randomized-controlled trial of individual versus couple-enhanced behavioral activation
summary:
Research has shown that psychotherapy is an effective treatment for depression. We also know that partnerships play an important role in mental health and the successful treatment of psychological disorder. That is why we want to use this study to investigate how involving partners in therapy affects the efficacy of depression treatment compared to therapy without the involvement of partners.
An effective technique widely used in behavioral therapy for the treatment of depression is behavioral activation. This will therefore be a focus of the therapy. The goal of behavioral activation is to (re)engage in activities that are personally important to you or that bring you joy. In therapy, we focus on your personal values and goals.
In addition, we want to use the collected data to investigate the relationships between various relationship factors, such as communication and mutual support, and depressive symptoms and the efficacy of therapy. The data from the surveys completed in daily life will provide us with valuable insights into the temporal associations between symptoms and individual dynamics. This will enable us to further develop treatment options for depression and hopefully offer even more tailored treatments in the future.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
a. Patient must be accepted for treatment at the outpatient clinic Marburg
b. Patient with primary diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder according to DSM-5 criteria  und BDI-II score >= 20
c. Currently in a committed relationship for at least 6 months
d. Living together or regular contact (some contact on at least 5 days/week)
e. Patients and partners willing to participate
f. Partners and patients willing and able to attend joint sessions if assigned to CE-BA
g. Both partners have sufficient German language skills in order to participate in the assessments and in treatment
h. Patients have to have public health insurance
i. Patients have consented to their participation in the Z-Project in DYNAMIC
Exclusion criteria:
a. High risk of harm to self or others
b. Intimate partner violence or threat of violence in the past year
c. Currently undergoing couple therapy or couples counseling
d. Anticipated changes of psychiatric medication during active treatment
e. Any psychosis or schizophrenia, unless stably remitted on maintenance therapy for at least 1 year
f. Developmental disability that would impair the ability to benefit from the intervention
